scenes.visual: 8.1.1: diagram maps task to the contract principle. 8.1.2: createTerminal with ompUi task lifecycle, Titanium, Unicode, band composer, no startup art or worker model badges. sentences.text: omp provides building blocks for these patterns, but its documentation is not evidence that an omp ensemble outperforms a single loop.
The task tool delegates to named specialists and can launch a batch in the background.
Children start without the parent’s conversation history, so shared context and self-contained assignments must carry what matters.
Give each specialist a concrete contract: scope, expected artifacts, evidence, dependencies, and completion criteria that another agent can actually use.

sentences.text: The bundled roster has five types: scout, reviewer, security-reviewer, task, and sonic; additional specialists can come from other definitions.
Fifteen built-in model roles separate the job from its concrete model assignment.
Here, explicit assignments connect roles to models across providers; treat this as a worked example rather than a recommended shopping list.
The terminal status uses friendly names; Agent Hub uses model IDs.
A scout’s small-model role is a routing choice, not proof that the chosen model is best for scouting.

scenes.title: Fan out, integrate deliberately
scenes.visual: 8.3.1: diagram sends bounded read-only scouts into parallel lanes. 8.3.2: separate optional edit lanes turn on task isolation with an explicit nondefault badge. 8.3.3–8.3.4: outputSchema cards carry paths and assumptions into one integration owner; label architectural mapping as inference.

sentences.text: Parallel scouts map naturally to separable investigations, returning focused evidence rather than repeatedly copying their entire exploration history.
Optional task isolation separates edits in Git workspaces for controlled integration; it is off by default.
Structured results can preserve artifact references and consequential decisions for the integration owner.
Keep one owner responsible for reconciling shared interfaces and assumptions before treating the separate contributions as an integrated result.

onScreen.text: Editorial mapping: separable work → scouts; ownership → integration owner; provenance → outputSchema + artifact references
Optional deviation: task.isolation.enabled: true; request isolated: true · Git required · shipped task.isolation.enabled: false · workspace separation, not sandboxing

scenes.title: Review versus verification
scenes.visual: 8.4.1: timeline with ompUi advisor card, advisor enabled explicitly labelled nondefault. Use the captured concern layout with illustrative text: Verify the greeting preserves empty-input behavior; keep Recreation · omp 18.8.6 defaults visible with the advisor-enabled exception. 8.4.2: contrast advice with an external-check gate. 8.4.3: diagram contrasts stateless completion, dependency waves of agent handles, reusable workpool, and judge. 8.4.4: typed-result outline stops before the factual verification gate.

sentences.text: An optional advisor reviews transcript updates and can investigate with read-only tools by default, sending concerns without becoming an approval authority.
Its advice still needs adjudication; additional mutating tool grants change the trust boundary.
Eval also offers tool-free completions, real agent handles, reusable workpools, and typed judgments.
A valid schema constrains shape, while a judge’s probability is not a calibrated guarantee of correctness.

onScreen.text: Advisor: opt-in; advisor.enabled defaults false · default investigative tools read-only · not approval authority
completion(): no tools/history · agent() + wait(handles): staged dependency waves · workpool(): reusable workers · judge(): typed assessment
Shape validation ≠ factual correctness · judgment probability ≠ calibrated guarantee

scenes.title: Autonomy is not confinement
scenes.visual: 8.6.1: safety statCard pins yolo default. 8.6.2: diagram shows explicit per-tool policies survive the headless boundary, with prompt failure rather than implied human forwarding. 8.6.3: distinguish workspace lanes from security perimeter. 8.6.4–8.6.5: separate concurrency controls and role availability selection versus request recovery.

sentences.text: The default approval mode is yolo, and headless task children explicitly run in yolo.
Explicit deny or prompt policies still matter; a required prompt without an interactive interface fails rather than granting permission.
Workspace isolation is not network, credential, or arbitrary filesystem confinement.
Task concurrency does not cap every eval agent or provider request.
Role candidate selection and request-failure fallback chains are separate mechanisms.

scenes.title: Not additional algorithms
scenes.visual: 8.7.1–8.7.2: diagram cards distinguish humans sharing one session from one session changing model. 8.7.3: return to the principles map; no performance chart.

sentences.text: Collab lets humans observe or steer a shared live session; it is not another autonomous-agent algorithm.
Prewalk hands a session from one model to another once, rather than creating parallel debaters.
Choose the primitive that fits your dependency graph, then measure the integrated outcome instead of assuming orchestration creates quality.

onScreen.text: Collab: humans share one running session · Prewalk: one-shot model handoff · neither is a multi-agent algorithm
